newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dow drags Russian shares lower, further falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Dow drags Russian shares lower, further falls seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares followed major world markets down on Monday in response to Friday's decline on Wall Street, and the downward trend looked set to continue on Tuesday, some traders said.
"Our market is very heavily dependent on movements on the Dow Jones -- it fell almost 150 points on Friday and Western sales are noticeable today," said Andrei Kukk, head of trading at Rinaco Plus.
The Russian Trading System index fell 2.5 percent to 287.76 at close on Tuesday from Friday's close of 294.94.
Oil company Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS ordinaries slipped to $0.684 from $0.726 at Friday's close.
Telecommunications company Rostelekom RTKM.RTS fell to $3.58 from $3.69.
"A number of shares fell below their support levels today and I think we're still going to see a 15-percent fall," said ING Baring senior trader Peter Kizenko.
But other traders said early buying in opening trade on Monday indicated current levels could be sustained on Tuesday.
"I don't think levels of support have been broken anywhere. The levels that have been achieved over the past month and a half will be very difficult to break through," said Kukk.
He said the market was unlikely to fall much in the next few days, although political developments could have an impact.
"Everyone will be watching the government's next steps regarding (natural gas company) Gazprom and (power utility) RAO UES," said Kukk.
The companies are at the heart of a government campaign, opposed by the State Duma, to restructure and tighten state regulation of the country's natural monopolies.
UES EESR.RTS ordinaries declined to $0.2009 from Friday's close of $0.2095, and Gazprom GAZP.RTS edged down to $0.620 from $0.630.

"If the government manages to conquer Gazprom, I would buy and buy and buy at current levels, because that will mean that the government is strong enough to see the job through to the end, and that the economic situation will improve," said Kukk.
Kizenko said new support levels could form by the end of this month and that demand for Russian securities would step up after the upcoming Victory Day holiday at the beginning of May.
